title: Image Formed by a Plane Mirror
subject: Physics
objective: Stand 2 m from a mirror and your image is 4 m from you. Why a plane mirror's image is virtual, erect, the same size, as far behind as you are in front, and laterally inverted.

fill.q: The image formed by a plane mirror is always ____ and erect.
The image is as far ____ the mirror as the object is in front of it.
The size of the image in a plane mirror is ____ the size of the object.
Right appearing as left in a mirror is called lateral ____.
If you stand 2 m from a plane mirror, your image is ____ m from you.

tf.q: A plane mirror's image can be caught on a screen.
tf.explain: It is virtual: the rays only appear to meet behind the mirror.

tf.q: The image becomes smaller as you move away from a plane mirror.
tf.explain: Its size stays the same; it only looks smaller because it is farther away.

tf.q: The image in a plane mirror is erect.
tf.explain: It is upright, the same way up as the object.

tf.q: The magnification of a plane mirror is 1.

ar.a: The image formed by a plane mirror is virtual.
ar.r: The reflected rays do not actually meet; their extensions meet behind the mirror.

ar.a: The letter "R" appears as "Я" in a plane mirror.
ar.r: A plane mirror laterally inverts the image.

mcq.q: You stand 5 m from a plane mirror. Your distance from your image is:
Which word is written laterally inverted on ambulances?
mcq.explain: So it reads correctly in a rear-view mirror.

mcq.q: The image in a plane mirror is:
mcq.explain: Rays appear to meet behind the mirror; it stays upright.

mcq.q: A person walks towards a mirror at 1 m/s. The image approaches the person at:
mcq.explain: Both move towards the mirror, so the gap closes twice as fast.

num.q: A candle is 30 cm in front of a plane mirror. It is moved 10 cm closer. Find the new distance between the candle and its image.
You stand 3 m from a mirror and step back 1 m. How far is your image from you now?

short.q: Draw and explain how a plane mirror forms the image of a point object.
short.solution: Two rays from the point reflect with i = r; the reflected rays diverge; extended backwards they meet behind the mirror at the virtual image, as far behind as the object is in front.

right: Cannot be caught on a screen
